extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting to biomedical journals; journal editors and publishers (ICMJE member and other medical journals)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for completing and implementing the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors (ICMJE) uniform conflict-of-interest disclosure form for biomedical journal submissions, and for journals adopting the form. Covers what to report, form structure, translation, technical deployment, and transition policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a uniform electronic disclosure form
rubrics_metrics.description: The ICMJE developed an electronic uniform disclosure form (placed in the public domain in October 2009) to reduce variability among journals in asking about and reporting authors' potential conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Member journals piloted the form and were encouraged to adopt it; other journals are invited to use it to lessen confusion for authors, readers, and the public. The revised/new form will be the standard for new submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report direct financial competing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Competing interests that involve the direct exchange of money from an interested party to an individual author or the author's institution should be reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Committee retained focus on direct financial exchanges as a definable core of competing interests, because these are clearer to identify than many indirect or nonfinancial associations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of spouse and minor-children queries
rubrics_metrics.description: Queries about potential competing interests of authors' spouses and minor children were removed from the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change was made in response to largely negative feedback and because asking about family members was seen as overly intrusive and difficult to define/implement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-ended reporting of other (nonfinancial/indirect) relationships (Section 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single open-ended query (new Section 4) asks: 'Are there any other relationships or activities that readers could perceive to influence, or that give the appearance of potentially influencing, what you wrote in the submitted work?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This places the onus on the person completing the form to identify and report appropriate nonfinancial competing interests. It is intended to be less intrusive than prior specific queries about nonfinancial associations while providing a locus for such disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearer wording and numeric designation of form fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Each field in the form now has a numeric designation and the language in the instructions and individual queries has been modified for clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbering fields and clarifying language aim to improve clarity for users and reduce misinterpretation; this change also supports translation and standard deployment across journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide glossary of terms and translation guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: To make the form more useful to non-native English speakers, the ICMJE is creating a glossary of terms used in the form and will post guidelines for translation of the form's instructions into multiple languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations must capture the essence of the queries rather than their literal meaning; glossary and instructions will be posted on www.icmje.org and translations added as they become available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical deployment requirement (Adobe Reader)
rubrics_metrics.description: The electronic form requires the user to download the free Adobe Reader, version 8.0 or higher, in order to function correctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical issues about correct deployment were raised during piloting; journals and users should be aware of this dependency to avoid access problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition policy for previously completed forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who have completed the older version of the form in conjunction with a journal submission need not complete the new form; the new form will be the standard for new submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy facilitates transition to the revised form while avoiding unnecessary duplication of effort for authors with ongoing submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative improvement via community feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: The ICMJE solicited and considered feedback from authors, editors, and other parties and anticipates modifying the form based on comments received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments were invited via the ICMJE website and the Committee planned to consider comments received before a specified date when preparing the next iteration. The document acknowledges complexity and expects further refinement over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: balance intrusiveness and completeness; avoid perfectionism
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes the complexity, subjectivity, and emotional nature of conflict disclosure; the Committee states it cannot let 'the perfect be the enemy of the good.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim is to simplify and standardize reporting to alleviate confusion and ease reporting burden on biomedical researchers, accepting that the instrument may not satisfy all critics in all respects.
